title: Pre-Focus Alignment Ritual
opening: Use this brief check when the link between the task and what matters is unclear. If the connection is already clear, begin the work directly.

labels.opportunity: What real opportunity is in front of you?
labels.valueGoal: What value does this serve, and what specific result would show progress?
labels.difficulty: What difficulty are you willing to accept for that result?
labels.work: What will you do in this work period? Begin it, or revise the task if the connection fails.
labels.example: Check the existing answer before making another one

actions.description: Point to what is actually available or needed now. A broad ambition is not the opportunity for this session.
actions.title: Name the opportunity

actions.description: Use the real relationship between this task and that result.
actions.title: Connect value to a goal

actions.description: Name the specific friction you are prepared to face because of that result. Do not pretend the task is meaningful if the link is missing.
actions.title: Choose the difficulty willingly

actions.description: Choose work small enough to start in this period. If it does not advance the stated goal, change the task or leave it undone.
actions.title: Set the work and begin, or revise

feedback.unavailable: Private saving is unavailable. Your draft remains here.
feedback.missing: Add a work action or a useful task revision before saving this draft.
feedback.readFailure: Your saved draft could not be loaded. Your current words remain here.
feedback.conflict: This draft changed elsewhere. Your answers remain here; compare the saved version before saving again.
feedback.readbackFailure: The save could not be confirmed. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.saveFailure: The save is uncertain. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.retryPending: The earlier save is unresolved. Retry the same draft before changing it.

source.manuscript: Manuscript p. 35 verified in the 82-page PDF from Trillion_X_Framework_Library/sources/Manuscript.pdf in Downloads/Trillion X Framework Library.zip. Archive member and retained copy match byte-for-byte (1,151,040 bytes; BLAKE3 d56f79b3e630df54d13ddf5a4868fe310d2acad25d3283de18ff7a5b3188c27e). The page heading is Pre-Focus Alignment Ritual; it asks the learner to state the opportunity, value, goal, accepted difficulty and specific work, then begin while those relationships are clear.
source.limits: The scenario is authored instructional material, not an observed learner result. The local Classroom run does not establish author acceptance, canonical adoption, publication, or learning effectiveness.

context.title: The opportunity
context.description: A billing team needs the current list of invoices awaiting review before its next meeting. A teammate suggests writing a new guide.

make.title: Write another guide now
make.description: This creates a second set of instructions before anyone checks whether the current invoice view already answers the question. Its relationship to the team's goal is unknown.

reuse.title: Inspect the existing invoice view first
reuse.description: Open the current view and check its owner, update time and whether it shows the invoices the team needs. If it does, point to that source. If it does not, record the exact gap and revise the task to address it.

examples.summary: The second option directly checks whether existing work already serves the goal. Making new material is justified only if the check finds a real gap.

practice.opportunity: Name the actual event, need or opening in front of you.
practice.valueGoal: Who benefits, and what concrete result should this work advance?
practice.difficulty: What inconvenient or demanding part are you choosing to face for that result?
practice.step: Write a small action you can start now, or the change you will make if it does not serve the goal.
